sources: IAL Command Word Expected Response Document

AO1.name: Knowledge and Understanding
AO1.description: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of economic concepts, theories and models

howToScore.fullMarks: Precise definition using correct economic terminology
howToScore.partialMarks: Basic understanding shown but lacks precision

AO2.name: Application
AO2.description: Apply knowledge and understanding to various economic contexts

howToScore.fullMarks: Clear application to the specific context/extract provided
howToScore.partialMarks: Some reference to context but lacks depth
howToScore.noMarks: Generic answer with no contextual application

AO3.name: Analysis
AO3.description: Analyse economic issues and arguments using appropriate methods

howToScore.fullMarks: Developed chains of reasoning with cause-effect relationships
howToScore.partialMarks: Some analysis but chains of reasoning incomplete

AO4.name: Evaluation
AO4.description: Evaluate economic arguments and evidence, making reasoned judgements

howToScore.fullMarks: Developed evaluation with chains of reasoning and informed judgement
howToScore.partialMarks: Evaluative points identified but not developed
howToScore.noMarks: No attempt at evaluation or purely descriptive

requirements: Definition only required
No examples needed from context
No application marks available

levelDescriptors.2marks: Comprehensive definition with excellent precision using correct terminology

examinerTips: Use exact economic terminology
Be concise and precise
Do not waste time adding examples unless asked

requirements: 1 mark for original supply and demand curves
1 mark for drawing the correct shift
1 mark for labelling new price
1 mark for labelling new quantity
examinerTips: Label axes clearly (Price on Y, Quantity on X)
Label all curves at the END of the line (D, S, D1, S1)
Use directional arrows to show shift direction
Label new equilibrium clearly (E to E1)
No written explanation required - diagram alone can achieve full marks

requirements: 1 mark for correct formula
3 marks for calculations and correct answer
examinerTips: Always show the formula first
Show all working out
Include units in final answer
PED is always negative - include negative sign
Elasticities are NOT percentages - do not add % sign
For change calculations, show if positive or negative

requirements: Knowledge and application only
No analysis marks

triggers: illustrate your answer with a diagram
requirements: Requires analysis
If diagram asked, 2 marks for diagram
Diagram if instructed: 1 K for original curves, 1 Ap for shift, 1 An for new equilibrium
Developed chains of reasoning required
NO evaluation marks available
examinerTips: Do NOT provide evaluation - no marks available
Focus on cause-effect chains
Use economic terminology precisely

requirements: Knowledge: definition + identifying factor from case study
Application and analysis: up to 2 marks per linked explanation (max 4)
Evaluation: 2 marks for 2 evaluative points OR 1 developed evaluation

levelDescriptors.level3: 7-8 marks: Strong knowledge, developed analysis, supported evaluation in context
levelDescriptors.level2: 4-6 marks: Sound knowledge, some analysis, limited evaluation
levelDescriptors.level1: 1-3 marks: Basic knowledge, weak analysis, no evaluation

examinerTips: Consider 3 factors maximum - more is excessive
Evaluation is REQUIRED for full marks
Many students fail to attempt evaluation
Avoid overwriting - timing is crucial

KAA.level3: 7-8 marks: Excellent knowledge, fully in context, developed chains of reasoning with accurate diagrams
KAA.level2: 4-6 marks: Sound knowledge, some context, basic analysis
KAA.level1: 1-3 marks: Generic answer with limited/no context

evaluation.level3: 5-6 marks: Developed chains of reasoning, fully in context, informed judgement
evaluation.level2: 3-4 marks: Some development of evaluative points

examinerTips: Context is VERY important for KAA
Generic answer = Level 1 only
Use extract data as starting point for evaluation
Write longer chains of reasoning for 2 points rather than 3 undeveloped points
Accurate diagram with explanation can shift Level 2 to Level 3
Include informed judgement for top marks

KAA.level3: 9-12 marks: Excellent knowledge, precise concepts, developed chains, accurate diagrams, full context
KAA.level2: 5-8 marks: Sound knowledge, some analysis, partial context
KAA.level1: 1-4 marks: Basic knowledge, limited analysis, no context

evaluation.level3: 7-8 marks: Developed chains of reasoning in context, informed judgement
evaluation.level2: 4-6 marks: Partially developed evaluation, some context

requirements: Clear essay structure with distinct paragraphs
NOT bullet points or long blocks without distinction
3-4 analysis points with development
3-4 evaluation points for full marks
Informed judgement required for Level 3 evaluation
examinerTips: Structure: clear paragraphs covering one issue each
Define key terms relevant to question
Include diagram if relevant and explain it
Depth over breadth: develop 2-3 points well rather than many superficially
Context from stem AND own examples
Chains of reasoning not just separate points
End with informed judgement based on evidence

CLASPP.L: Long run vs Short run impact

chainsOfReasoning.definition: A logical sequence of cause-effect statements that shows economic understanding
chainsOfReasoning.example: Factor X → Causes Y → Which leads to Z → Therefore outcome W
requirements: Each step must follow logically from the previous
Use connective phrases: 'this leads to', 'as a result', 'consequently', 'therefore'
Include economic concepts at each step
Apply to the specific context given

templates.demand_increase: Increase in [factor] → Increases demand → D curve shifts right → Creates shortage at original price → Price bid up → Movement along supply → New equilibrium at higher P and Q
templates.externality: [Activity] creates [external cost/benefit] → MSC ≠ MPC (or MSB ≠ MPB) → Market equilibrium ≠ Social optimum → Over/under production → Welfare loss → Market failure
templates.monetary_policy: Central bank [raises/lowers] interest rates → Cost of borrowing [increases/decreases] → Consumer spending and investment [falls/rises] → AD [decreases/increases] → Inflationary pressure [reduced/increased]

gradingBehavior.rationale: Promotes better learning outcomes while remaining fair

definitions.fullMarks: Only for precise, technically correct definitions
definitions.deductions: Missing key terms, imprecise language, unnecessary elaboration

analysis.fullMarks: Complete chains of reasoning with economic terminology
analysis.deductions: Broken chains, missing steps, descriptive rather than analytical

evaluation.fullMarks: Developed points with context and judgement
evaluation.deductions: Listing points without development, generic statements, no judgement

diagrams.fullMarks: Correctly drawn, fully labelled, referenced in text
diagrams.deductions: Unlabelled axes, wrong direction shifts, not explained

context.required: For any marks above Level 1 in discuss/evaluate questions

general: Providing evaluation when not asked (e.g., in 'analyse' questions)
Overwriting on shorter questions, leaving no time for essays
Writing in bullet points for essay questions
diagrams: Not labelling new curves differently (S to S1)
Confusing movement along vs shift of curve
calculations: Not showing whether change is positive/negative
essays: No diagram when one would help
Separate points without chains of reasoning

feedbackTemplates.good: Good attempt showing understanding of key concepts. To improve: {improvement}
feedbackTemplates.satisfactory: Basic understanding shown but lacking {missing_element}. Focus on developing {skill}
